pages.lesson:
LESSON: INTENSIVE READING 4.4.1 PLAY: IDENTIFICATION OF CHARACTERS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.4: Intensive Reading 4.4.1 Play: Identification of Characters

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Intensive Reading 4.4.1 Play: Identification of Characters. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can one tell the qualities of a character in a play?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the characters in a play
2. use appropriate adjectives to describe the characters
3. describe the actions of the characters using appropriate adverbs
4. value the need to describe people and situations appropriately

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: INTENSIVE READING 4.4.1 PLAY: IDENTIFICATION OF CHARACTERS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Intensive Reading 4.4.1 Play: Identification of Characters helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: INTENSIVE READING 4.4.1 PLAY: IDENTIFICATION OF CHARACTERS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the characters in a play

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the characters in a play. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the characters in a play.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Intensive Reading 4.4.1 Play: Identification of Characters”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the characters in a play. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use appropriate adjectives to describe the characters

What this means
In this part you learn to use appropriate adjectives to describe the characters. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use appropriate adjectives to describe the characters.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Intensive Reading 4.4.1 Play: Identification of Characters to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use appropriate adjectives to describe the characters. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Describe the actions of the characters using appropriate adverbs

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the actions of the characters using appropriate adverbs. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the actions of the characters using appropriate adverbs.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the actions of the characters using appropriate adverbs. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Value the need to describe people and situations appropriately

What this means
In this part you learn to value the need to describe people and situations appropriately. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value the need to describe people and situations appropriately.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Intensive Reading 4.4.1 Play: Identification of Characters”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value the need to describe people and situations appropriately. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Intensive Reading 4.4.1 Play: Identification of Characters is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Intensive Reading 4.4.1 Play: Identification of Characters”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the characters in a play)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Intensive Reading 4.4.1 Play: Identification of Characters to a partner. (skill: use appropriate adjectives to describe the characters)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: describe the actions of the characters using appropriate adverbs)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Intensive Reading 4.4.1 Play: Identification of Characters”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: value the need to describe people and situations appropriately)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Intensive Reading 4.4.1 Play: Identification of Characters to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the characters in a play.
3. Practise this skill: use appropriate adjectives to describe the characters.
4. Practise this skill: describe the actions of the characters using appropriate adverbs.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Intensive Reading 4.4.1 Play: Identification of Characters from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Intensive Reading 4.4.1 Play: Identification of Characters: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Intensive Reading 4.4.1 Play: Identification of Characters?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can one tell the qualities of a character in a play?
2. How does describing actions of characters aid our understanding of a play?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Intensive Reading 4.4.1 Play: Identification of Characters means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the characters in a play.
5. Be able to: use appropriate adjectives to describe the characters.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
